questions.question: What are the three memory tiers in Letta?
options: Cache, Store, Archive
Core (always visible), Recall (conversation history), Archival (external facts)
Short-term, Medium-term, Long-term
Hot, Warm, Cold
questions.explanation: Letta organizes memory into three tiers: Core (always visible in the prompt, managed by agent tools and sleep-time rewrites), Recall (conversation history with retrievable evicted tail), and Archival (external vector+KV+graph store).

questions.question: What are the two default memory blocks in the original MemGPT paper?
options: System block and User block
Human block and Persona block
Task block and History block
Input block and Output block
questions.explanation: The original MemGPT paper defined two memory blocks: Human block (facts about the user: name, role, preferences) and Persona block (the agent's self-concept: identity, tone, constraints). Letta generalizes to arbitrary user-defined blocks.

questions.question: What are the three key advantages of sleep-time compute running off the critical path?
options: Lower cost, faster models, more accurate results
No latency cost for primary agent, stronger model allowed, natural consolidation window
Easier debugging, simpler code, better observability
Less memory usage, faster retrieval, cleaner API
questions.explanation: Sleep-time compute running off the critical path means: no latency cost (primary responses don't wait), a stronger/more expensive model can be used (no latency constraint), and there is a natural window to deduplicate, summarize, and invalidate contradicted facts.

questions.question: What does 'silent drift' mean in the context of memory blocks?
options: The block slowly fills up with useless information
The sleep-time agent rewrites a block and the primary agent never notices the change
The agent gradually loses accuracy over time
Memory blocks are not persisted between sessions
questions.explanation: Silent drift occurs when the sleep-time agent rewrites a block but the primary agent continues operating without awareness of the change. Mitigation: version blocks and surface diffs in the trace.

questions.question: What key change does Letta V1 make compared to the original MemGPT loop?
options: Removes the memory blocks concept entirely
Replaces send_message/heartbeat and inline Thought: tokens with native reasoning via the Responses/Messages API
Adds a fourth memory tier
Migrates from Python to TypeScript
questions.explanation: Letta V1 (letta_v1_agent, 2026) deprecates the old send_message/heartbeat pattern and explicit Thought: token scheme in favor of native reasoning — emitted on a separate channel and passed through turns encrypted in production.

questions.question: What happens when a memory block approaches its character limit?
options: New writes are silently discarded
The agent should call block_summarize to condense the block before the next write pushes it over the cap
The system automatically deletes the oldest entries
The block resets to its initial state
questions.explanation: Each block has a limit (character cap). When a block is near its limit, the agent should call block_summarize to condense the block value; otherwise the next append will overflow and be rejected.
